en.headline: Police receive 216 reports totaling HK$38 million over closed luxury consignment shops
en.dek: Reports concerning Vootic in Causeway Bay and Obsessplanet in Admiralty rose sharply, with police classifying the cases as fraud and seeking a Japanese owner.
body: Police said they had received reports from 216 people alleging unpaid consignment payments totaling about HK$38 million after two second-hand luxury goods shops closed abruptly.

Officers said 140 reports related to Vootic on Russell Street in Causeway Bay involving roughly HK$26.5 million, while 76 reports concerned Obsessplanet on Harcourt Road in Admiralty involving about HK$11.5 million.

The cases have been classified as fraud and are being handled by the Wan Chai and Central district crime squads, police said. The Japanese owner and his wife have been reported unreachable, and investigators are seeking their whereabouts.
Customers and other shops that had left merchandise for sale said they could not retrieve goods or payments after the outlets stopped responding and shut their doors earlier in the week.

zh.headline: 警方接獲216宗報案涉款3800萬 兩間名牌寄賣店結業
zh.dek: 銅鑼灣Vootic及金鐘樂星寄賣店結業後報案人數急增，警方暫列欺詐，正追緝日籍負責人。
body: 警方表示，截至周三傍晚，已接獲216人報案，指兩間二手名牌寄賣店拖欠寄賣款項，涉及總金額約3800萬元。
警方指，其中140人報案涉及銅鑼灣羅素街Vootic，涉款約2650萬元；另有76人報案涉及金鐘夏懒道樂星（Obsessplanet），涉款約1150萬元。
案件暫列欺詐，由灣仔警區重案組及中區警區重案組跟進。有報案人指日籍東主及其妻子失聯，警方正設法追查其下落。
多名寄賣客戶及同行表示，店舖本周初起不再回覆訊息後拉閘結業，未能取回寄賣貨品或已售款項。
